objections.claim: This is two changes wearing one ticket: a small reporting fix, and the first real exercise of the code-blind holdout path. The spec's own scenarios embed two `holdout` blocks whose purpose is not to verify FAFF-1354 but to prove FAFF-1270's evaluator pipeline works — including one that requires the evaluator env to pass a literal line feed inside a `--kernel` argv argument, a capability the spec itself admits may not exist.
objections.evidence: Methodology critique, Risk: "This build also serves as FAFF-1270's code-blind holdout proving run… The second holdout needs the evaluator to pass a literal line feed inside a `--kernel` argument, which a code-blind judge driving a running env may not be able to express." Also section 5's two `holdout` scenarios, one of which (`bad<newline>kernel`) is precisely the harness-stumble case.
objections.predicted_consequence: A harness stumble stalls a small, independently valuable fix and leaves FAFF-1270 with a failed proving run of ambiguous cause — the critique's own words. The slice's merge becomes hostage to an unrelated pipeline's first-run reliability.
objections.disposition_rationale: Fixed in spec round 2: the line-feed holdout became a visible scenario and both holdouts now drive only the CLI; section 7 records that a harness-traced holdout failure is filed against FAFF-1270 or FAFF-1346.

objections.claim: The edge case "`--kernel` contains a newline or tab" (edge-case table) and its DONE-adjacent behaviour (stderr stays one line, note's `kernel` collapsed) have exactly one scenario — a `holdout` scenario that requires the code-blind evaluator to pass a shell argument containing a raw line feed. The spec's own Methodology critique section says this "a code-blind judge driving a running env may not be able to express" and recommends swapping it for a `claim-verdict`-style scenario, yet section 5 still ships it as a holdout. If the harness cannot express the argument, that named edge case has no test anywhere: the visible integration tests cover only the non-holdout scenarios, and no DONE bullet asserts the newline case outside the holdout.
objections.evidence: Section 5, second `holdout` scenario; edge-case table row "`--kernel` contains a newline or tab"; Methodology critique → Risk, first bullet.
objections.predicted_consequence: The line-safe collapsing behaviour for control characters in `kernel` (a core part of the new `lineSafe` contract) can ship untested if the proving harness stumbles, and a failed holdout is ambiguous between "build wrong" and "harness can't express the input" — the spec pre-agrees to file such a result against FAFF-1270/FAFF-1346, so the edge case silently ends up with no verdict at all.
objections.disposition_rationale: Fixed in spec round 2: the --kernel line-feed case is a visible scenario and a Done item, no longer holdout-only.
